newsitem.title: VATICAN: Work is a fundamental right, says Pope.
newsitem.headline: Work is a fundamental right, says Pope.

text.p: Pope John Paul said on Monday that people had a fundamental right to work and criticised what he said was the shameless exploitation of workers, including women and children, in some parts of the world.

The 76-year-old Pontiff, who was addressing trades unionists from around the world taking part in a two-day meeting on labour at the Vatican, also cautioned that economic efficiency had to respect employment and not be motivated only by profit.
He told the trades union leaders that their organisations had a continued role to play "in building a truly just and democratic world" through dialogue and cooperation.

"In the dynamic and changing context of today's economy, the right to work has to be reaffirmed as a fundamental right, corresponding to people's fundamental responsibility to support themselves and their families," the Pope said.

He said that while the demand for greater economic efficiency was "inevitable and legitimate", the "tragic and often unjust situation of those who do not find work, or have lost it, must be a major concern".

"At the same time, how can we not recall the ways in which workers in some parts of the world are made the object of shameless exploitation, often as a result of ideas of the economy which disregard every moral value?" he asked.
"How can we not condemn the unacceptable behaviour of those, who, even in some regions with a solid industrial base, exploit the work of women and especially of children?"
The Pope has frequently spoken of a special affinity he has with workers from his years working in a stone quarry in his native Poland during World War Two.
He was a major influence in the collapse of communism in Poland and elsewhere in eastern Europe but has not shied from criticising what he sees as the excesses of capitalism.
